heading: INT. GENERATION SHIP "HALCYON REACH" - HYDROPONICS RING - SHIP'S NIGHT

units.text: INT. GENERATION SHIP "HALCYON REACH" - HYDROPONICS RING - SHIP'S NIGHT
A curved corridor of green.
Racks of lettuce and soy climb the walls under violet grow-lamps.
Condensation beads on every pipe.
Far below the deck plates, the ship's engines pulse like a slow heart.
COMMANDER ISOLDE VARGAS-ABIOLA, fifties, stands at a junction with her arms folded, still in her night robe.
Her first officer, TOMASZ BRZEZINSKI, forties, has a hand tablet and a scowl.
The agronomist, DR. NADIA OKONKWO-REID, thirties, kneels at a rack with a soil probe.
The boy, KAI SOLOMON, twelve, lingers behind a tank with a bucket.
A maintenance tech, FEODOR LINDGREN, sixty, sits cross-legged on the deck with a panel open.
And the ship's counselor, PRIYANKA ADEYEMI, forties, hangs back at the corridor mouth.
The grow-lamps flicker.
Every leaf in the corridor turns, slowly, toward the same direction.
Tell me that isn't what I think it is.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: It's phototropism. Plants turn toward light.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: There is no light there.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: No. There isn't.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Tomasz looks up from his tablet.
Feodor taps his panel, and a weak amber glow pulses from the wiring.
He snatches his hand away.
Kai edges closer to the tank.
Commander, the sensors show the hull is clear. No breach. No micrometeorites.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Then why are my lettuces looking at the aft bulkhead?
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: Something's behind it.
units.name: FEODOR

units.text: There's nothing behind it. It's a bulkhead.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Then something's inside it.
units.name: FEODOR

units.text: Perhaps we should all take a breath.
units.name: PRIYANKA

units.text: I'm breathing, Priyanka. It isn't helping.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: Kai steps out from behind the tank, bucket swinging.
Mother says the walls have been singing since the last jump.
units.name: KAI

units.text: Kai, go to your quarters.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: I'm not afraid.
units.name: KAI

units.text: I didn't say you were.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: Commander. The plants aren't only turning. Look at the stems. They're growing toward it. Measurably, in real time.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: She holds up the probe.
A readout glows.
Tomasz crosses to her side, looks at it, and goes pale.
That's twenty centimeters in five minutes.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: It's accelerating.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: The corridor hums.
A low tone rises in the deck plates.
The violet lamps dim.
And from the aft bulkhead, through the steel, a pale seam of light begins to spread, slow as water, ruffling every leaf.
Is that...
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: It's alive.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Tomasz and Nadia speak at the same time, their words overlapping, and then stop, each turning toward the other.
Isolde steps forward, one hand lifted as if to touch the light.
Nobody move.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: Priyanka crosses herself in the old way.
Feodor scrambles to his feet.
Kai drops the bucket, and it clangs, and the sound echoes down the corridor and returns altered, almost a word.
It said "hello."
units.name: KAI

units.text: Kai.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: It did. It said hello.
units.name: KAI

units.text: Isolde kneels beside the boy and takes him by the shoulders.
Kai, look at me. Did you hear anything else?
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: It said it was lonely.
units.name: KAI

units.text: Silence.
The light stops spreading.
A single tendril of green curls out from the nearest rack and brushes the boy's sleeve, gentle as a child's hand.
Tomasz. Seal the corridor. Priyanka, get the captain. Nadia.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: Yes, Commander?
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Find out what it wants.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: And if it wants nothing?
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Then we will be very polite to it.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: Isolde rises, and the seam of light flickers once in answer, and every leaf in the corridor turns to face her.
